readings.eruv_declaration: בְּדֵן עֵרוּבָא יְהֵא שְׁרֵא לָנָא לְמֵיפָא וּלְבַשָּׁלָא וּלְאַטְמָנָא וּלְאַדְלָקָא שְׁרָגָא וּלְמֶעְבַּד כָּל־צָרְכָּנָא מִיּוֹמָא טָבָא לְשַׁבְּתָא לָנוּ וּלְכָל־הַדָּרִים בָּעִיר הַזֹּאת׃
readings.lekhah_dodi_rubric: הש"ץ מנגן בנעימה. | ראשי החרוזים שלמה הלוי.

poem_stanzas.text: לְכָה דוֹדִי לִקְרַאת כַּלָּה. פְּנֵי שַׁבָּת נְקַבְּלָה׃
שָׁמוֹר וְזָכוֹר בְּדִבּוּר אֶחָד. הִשְׁמִיעָנוּ אֵל הַמְיֻחָד. יְיָ אֶחָד וּשְׁמוֹ אֶחָד. לְשֵׁם וּלְתִפְאֶרֶת וְלִתְהִלָּה׃
לִקְרַאת שַׁבָּת לְכוּ וְנֵלְכָה. כִּי הִיא מְקוֹר הַבְּרָכָה. מֵרֹאשׁ מִקֶּדֶם נְסוּכָה. סוֹף מַעֲשֶׂה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה׃
מִקְדַּשׁ מֶלֶךְ עִיר מְלוּכָה. קוּמִי צְאִי מִתּוֹךְ הַהֲפֵכָה. רַב לָךְ שֶׁבֶת בְּעֵמֶק הַבָּכָא. וְהוּא יַחֲמוֹל עָלַיִךְ חֶמְלָה׃
הִתְנַעֲרִי מֵעָפָר קוּמִי. לִבְשִׁי בִּגְדֵי תִפְאַרְתֵּךְ עַמִּי. עַל־יַד בֶּן־יִשַׁי בֵּית הַלַּחְמִי. קָרְבָה אֶל־נַפְשִׁי גְאָלָהּ׃
הִתְעוֹרְרִי הִתְעוֹרְרִי. כִּי בָא אוֹרֵךְ קוּמִי אוֹרִי. עוּרִי עוּרִי שִׁיר דַּבֵּרִי. כְּבוֹד יְיָ עָלַיִךְ נִגְלָה׃
לֹא תֵבֹשִׁי וְלֹא תִכָּלְמִי. מַה תִּשְׁתּוֹחֲחִי וּמַה תֶּהֱמִי. בָּךְ יֶחֱסוּ עֲנִיֵּי עַמִּי. וְנִבְנְתָה עִיר עַל־תִּלָּהּ׃
וְהָיוּ לִמְשִׁסָּה שֹׁאסָיִךְ. וְרָחֲקוּ כָּל־מְבַלְּעָיִךְ. יָשִׂישׂ עָלַיִךְ אֱלֹהָיִךְ. כִּמְשׂוֹשׂ חָתָן עַל־כַּלָּה׃
יָמִין וּשְׂמֹאל תִּפְרוֹצִי. וְאֶת־יְיָ תַּעֲרִיצִי. עַל יַד־אִישׁ בֶּן־פַּרְצִי. וְנִשְׂמְחָה וְנָגִילָה׃
בּוֹאִי בְשָׁלוֹם עֲטֶרֶת בַּעְלָהּ. גַּם בְּשִׂמְחָה וּבְצָהֳלָה. תּוֹךְ אֱמוּנֵי עַם סְגֻלָּה. בּוֹאִי כַלָּה. בּוֹאִי כַלָּה׃

observations: s13 eruv: the blessing printed just before the declaration reads בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו וְצִוָּנוּ עַל מִצְוַת עֵרוּב׃. The declaration starts with a large initial בְּדֵן. The English margin cue is ברן, which looks like a misprint or a broken letter for בדן.
s13 eruv: the line breaks fall at כָּל־ / צָרְכָּנָא and at לְשַׁבְּתָא / לָנוּ. The text has לָנָא right after שְׁרֵא and לָנוּ near the end; it is not לָנָא in both places.

Lekhah Dodi rubric: two tiny unpointed parts on one line. The right-hand part is הש"ץ (with gershayim) מנגן בנעימה. The left-hand part is ראשי החרוזים שלמה הלוי. ראשי and החרוזים are spelled out in full; the only abbreviation is הש"ץ.

A small marginal לכה is printed beside the full opening refrain and after each of stanzas 1 to 9. All nine stanzas are inside these crops: the refrain and stanza 1 on s16-rubric, stanzas 1 (end) to 7 on s16-poem, stanzas 8 and 9 on s17-top.

Divine Names: the full Name יהוה is printed in Ps 29 (s16-ps29) and Ps 92/93 (s17-ps92, s17-bottom, s17-top). In every case I can make out, there is a sheva under the yod and a qamatz under the vav. Nothing is under the first he and nothing is under the final he. I could not see a holam dot over or near the he/vav in any instance at this resolution.
Prefixed full Name: Ps 92:2 (s17-top) reads לַיהוָה: patah under the lamed, no vowel on the yod (the sheva drops after the prefix), qamatz under the vav, and no holam seen.

Double-yod abbreviation: Ps 95:1 (s13-ps95) reads נְרַנְּנָה לַיְיָ. Unprefixed יְיָ (sheva under the first yod, qamatz under the second) appears in Ps 95, the eruv blessing, and Lekhah Dodi stanzas 1, 5 and 8.

Human clarification, not read from the scan: the user has confirmed that the opening cue also requires a congregational repeat of the refrain. This is a recitation-order instruction from the user. The scan only shows the marginal לכה beside the opening refrain.
uncertainties: לְמֵיפָא: the vowel under the pe is unclear. It could be a qamatz or a tsere, and I can't tell whether there is a dagesh. I gave the qamatz reading because it fits the glyph best, but this could be the customary form rather than what is printed.
צָרְכָּנָא: what looks like a dagesh is printed in the kaf (the customary text is צָרְכָנָא without one). Under the tsadi the mark looks like a qamatz, but it is smudged.
עֵרוּבָא: the vowel under the ayin looks like a tsere. A hataf vowel can't be completely ruled out.

Holam in the full Name: I saw no holam, but the dot is very small and the crops are compressed, so a faint holam could be missed. A higher-resolution check of one clean instance would settle it, e.g. Ps 29:3 קוֹל יְהוָה עַל־הַמָּיִם.
לַיְיָ (Ps 95:1): the sheva under the first yod after the prefix lamed is faint. The form could be לַייָ.

Rubric: the type is tiny. The first word of the second part is most likely ראשי, but the first letters are crowded together. The two parts are spaced apart on the line, so I can't confirm whether they are meant to be read as one rubric or two.

Poem pointing: I checked the consonants carefully. Small vowels such as hataf versus simple vowels, or dagesh in בְשָׁלוֹם and כַלָּה, are read as well as the resolution allows. Where a mark was illegible, the customary pointing may have filled in the gap, especially בֶּן־יִשַׁי, שֹׁאסָיִךְ and בְּצָהֳלָה.
